title: Latency budget scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tracker for small latency/cost experiments — focused on tiny config tweaks (batch, kv cache flag, quant) and their P50/P95 impact on short sequences (32-128). Not a formal spreadsheet, just a fast log I can scan and act on.

Table: (CSV-like for quick paste)
run_id, date, model, quant, kv_cache_enabled, batch_size, avg_seq, p50_ms, p95_ms, tok_per_sec, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, notes
R-001, 2024-04-18, llama-2-13b, fp16, true, 4, 32, 42, 98, 1600, 0.89, baseline single-shard, warm cache
R-002, 2024-04-19, llama-2-13b, int8, true, 4, 32, 36, 82, 1850, 0.71, ~15% p50 improvement, slight token/sec up
R-003, 2024-04-20, llama-2-13b, int8, false, 4, 32, 58, 140, 1100, 0.95, KV off regresses p95 a lot, p50 also worse
R-004, 2024-05-02, gptx-oculus-7b, int8, true, 8, 64, 51, 120, 1200, 0.45, batch 8 -> p50 up but p95 similar
R-005, 2024-05-09, llama-2-13b, int8, true, 1, 16, 24, 60, 2100, 0.54, low batch wins latency for short convo replies
R-006, 2024-08-21, llama-2-13b, q4_0, true, 4, 32, 40, 95, 1700, 0.62, q4_0 stable but watch occasional decoding slowdowns
R-007, 2024-09-14, llama-2-13b, q4_0, true, 16, 128, 160, 420, 320, 2.1, throughput test only (cost calc per 1M tokens unrealistic for small runs)

Quick observations:
- KV cache dramatically improves p95 for multi-turn scenarios when enabled; disabling it doubles p95 on several runs (R-003).
- Quant (int8 / q4_0) is a predictable win for p50, but watch out for p95 tail events on some workloads (rare decoding stalls).
- Small batch_size (1-4) is best for low-latency interactive flows; larger batches only help throughput for async batch jobs.
- Sequence length dominates cost: 4x seq ~= ~4x tokens, so prefer prefix caching and truncated prompts.

Quick commands I ran (for reproducibility):
- rwdctl run --model llama-2-13b --quant int8 --batch 4 --kv true --seq 32 --trials 50 --tag R-002
- rwdctl collect-metrics --run R-002 --out r-002-metrics.json
- jq '.latency | {p50: .p50, p95: .p95, tps: .tokens_per_sec}' r-002-metrics.json

Actionable next experiments (short list):
- A1: Compare int8 vs q4_0 on 13b with warm KV at batch sizes 1,4,8 (measure memory shifts + p95)
- A2: Run a jitter test (burstiness) with lambda-style small requests (simulate concurrent users)
- A3: Instrument kernel selection flag to force fallback kernels and measure impact (LINK: GH PR 812)

Mini budget calc (hand napkin):
- Target interactive SLO: p95 < 120ms for 32-token average sequences.
- From runs: int8+KV+batch4 gives p95 ~82-95ms (R-002 / R-006) -> acceptable.
- Cost rough: if tokens_per_sec ~ 1800, 1M tokens ~= 556s -> cost per 1M tokens = service price * factor. I used internal mapping to estimate 0.7-0.9 USD per 1M depending on reserved vs hosted.

Open questions / loose notes:
- Need a small harness to run longer tails (10k requests) to capture rare p99 decoding stalls.
- Confirm cost model for Dedicated vs Hosted for identical kernel/quant profiles.
- Check whether kernel selection metric is surfaced in Console trace (if not, file quick request with SRE).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Convert R-002/R-006 into a short blurb for PR with perf graphs (attach to PR 812).
- [ ] Add harness for jitter tests and schedule overnight run.
- [ ] Sync with Ravi re: cluster pinning for Dedicated sim.

Freeform notes (brain-dump):
- If we could make small auto-retries for decoding stalls (non-deterministic), that may reduce p95 cost of enabling aggressive quant. But that changes semantics; maybe better to fallback to fp16 on stall. Could implement as a transient-fallback policy.
- Remember: user-visible latency matters more than raw per-token costs for PLG features; optimize for p95 under 100ms for chat UX.

End of sheet.
